label: J1_grip_up
note: planner_alat is itself a joint move: it raises the corner-speed target (v_curve) AND the in-corner throttle cap (fc_frac) coherently. Paired with the sharply-targeted wheelspin guard, which fires on only 0.20% of ticks for a 185x sideslip-risk lift, i.e. near-free insurance.

label: J2_demand_down
note: THE UNTESTED DIRECTION. The bot is 13.4 km/h below its own target, so desired = kp_thr*err saturates and the throttle is shaped by the cap, not the controller. Lower the demand to something reachable AND give it more permission to reach it: a controller tracking an achievable target may drive better than one permanently saturated against an impossible one.

label: J3_grip_up_guarded
note: More demand, paid for with a tighter combined ceiling. slip_target 0.85 alone was STABLE after pad_clamp (sideslip p99 7.40 vs 7.30 baseline) but cost more throttle than it returned; here the tightening is paid back by the higher grip model rather than being a pure tax.
